svg.text: RESEARCH ETHICS — CONSENT IS A CONVERSATION, NOT A SIGNATURE
Approval comes before recruitment. A study begun without it cannot be made ethical afterwards.

g.text: INFORMED — purpose, procedures, risks, benefits, in a language the person actually speaks
VOLUNTARY — no pressure from the nurse, the doctor, the chief or the employer
CAPACITY — the person can understand, weigh and retain the information
WITHDRAWAL — may stop at any time, without giving a reason and without losing any care
cannot tell who gave the answer
and undertakes not to reveal it
Children, and those who lack capacity
Anyone who may feel unable to refuse you
Your own patient is asked to join your study. She may agree because you nurse her, not because she wishes to.
Separate the two roles: someone else takes consent, refusal is invisible to you, and her care changes in no way.

svg.text: Fabricating data, copying another author's words, or adding a friend as an author are all research misconduct.
If a participant would be upset to learn how her data was used, consent was never really obtained.
